# Themes

There are **9 themes** (presets), in this order (never reorder them): Fabrik, Illuzion, Laroc, Bootshaus, Berghain, Savaya, Pacha, Amnesia, Ushuaia. The default is **Berghain** (`DEFAULT_THEME_ID`). Source: `packages/ui/src/themes/presets.ts`; the model is `themes/types.ts`. Every preset has the same `feel` (all "none") and Phosphor regular icons, and answers "a" to all four UX-direction questions.

## The settings every theme has

| Setting | Options | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `colorMode` | light, dark | Which alpha wash and glass tone to use (light themes wash with dark, dark themes with light). One setting, no second light/dark switch. |
| `palette` | 7 colours + 5 chart colours | background, foreground, primary, primaryForeground, secondary, secondaryForeground, destructive, charts[5]. All the other colour tokens are derived from these. |
| `fonts` | display, body, secondary | Three roles. Each has family, weight, optional emphasis weight, letterSpacing (% of size), italic. Body also has actionWeight (button text) and lineHeight (%). |
| `scale` | sm, md, lg | Which typescale set is used (sizes in the Tokens reference). |
| `spacing` | sm, md, lg | Layout spacing between components only; component padding stays fixed. Carried as `--theme-spacing`; components do not read it yet. |
| `radius` | sharp, subtle, strong, rounded | sharp = square, subtle, strong, rounded = pill controls. |
| `shadow` | none, subtle, strong | Strength of every `shadow-*` token. |
| `material` (texture) | solid, glass, gradient | How cards and controls are made: solid wash, top-to-bottom gradient, or blurred glass. |
| `motion` (Component Animations) | none, ease, emphatic, springy | Easing and duration for every component transition. |
| `icons` | style: phosphor, lucide; weight: thin, light, regular, bold, fill, duotone | Icon family and weight. |
| `feel.transition` | none, blinds, iris, curtain, fade, curtain-iris | Page transition; plus colour (foreground, primary) and speed (slow, medium, fast). |
| `feel.animatedBackground` | none, aurora, smoke, ascii, holo, eighties | Plus themeColors, inverse and overlay (8, 24, 40, 56, 64, 80 %). |
| `feel.heroHeading` / `heroText` | none, gradient, shimmering / none, rolling, scramble, typewriter, splitting, vertical-cut | Hero section effects. |
| `feel.buttonClick` | none, ring, ripple, crosshair, burst, particles | Click effect on buttons. |
| `feel.linkHover` | none, underline, highlight | Link hover effect. |
| `values` | 4 answers, a or b | The UX direction (below). |

## UX direction (`values`)

Four questions, each answered a or b. They tell an AI how the product should behave, not how it looks.

- **How should people find their way around?** a = Guided (We show you the way, step by step.) · b = Exploratory (We let you look around and find your own way.)
- **Who should make the decisions?** a = Automated (We do things for you so you don't have to.) · b = In control (You decide what happens and when.)
- **Should it be quick to use, or packed with options?** a = Simple (You only see what you need right now.) · b = Powerful (Everything you might need is within reach.)
- **How should we talk to people?** a = Casual (We talk to you like a friend.) · b = Professional (We keep things to the point.)

## How a theme becomes CSS

`themeToCss(theme)` (themes/css.ts) writes one block scoped to `.<id>` (the default also on `:where(:root)`). `ThemeProvider` puts the class on `<html>`. The Themer downloads the same output, so what is downloaded is what the app renders. The resolved token list for every theme is in `themes-resolved.md`.
